| 11 | Material → stacked checkbox-group | **Not delivered** | Same as above — only `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:112-120`'s `MaterialPlaceholder` mock exists. Nothing in `product-list/index.tsx` special-cases or guarantees Material renders; it would only appear if/when SFCC returns a `material`-shaped refinement (SFCC-104 dependent). |
| 12 | Sleeve Length → stacked checkbox-group | **Not delivered** | Same pattern — `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:122-130`'s `SleeveLengthPlaceholder` mock only. |
| 13 | CLEAR (Secondary) + APPLY (Primary), Button-group layout=Inline | **Delivered** | `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:63-66`: two `ZimmButton`s (`variant="secondary"`/`"primary"`) side by side in a footer row. |
| 14 | WCAG 2.1 AA: accordion label+state, keyboard, CLEAR purposeful label | **Substantially delivered (not independently audited)** | `aria-expanded` confirmed (AC6 evidence); `zimmCheckbox/index.tsx:32` and `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:30` set `aria-label` via `ADD_FILTER`/`REMOVE_FILTER`; CLEAR's accessible name resolves to the literal string "CLEAR" (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:64`, `zimmButton/index.tsx:178`) — a real, non-empty label, though not obviously more "purposeful" than the visible text. ## 2. Radio vs checkbox — confirmed from source

The Category facet renders a plain Chakra `Checkbox`, not a `Radio`: `pr117-head/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:710-727`, using the base `Checkbox` imported at line 42 from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui`. `Radio`/`RadioGroup` are imported (lines 40-41) but never rendered anywhere in this file (confirmed by grep — their only other occurrence is a comment at line 566 about a *different*, unrelated OOTB `RadioRefinement` code path). Single-select is enforced only in JS state (`pendingCategoryId` is a scalar, not an array — `handleCategoryChange`, line 525), not via the native radio-button semantics AC2/AC3 ask for. This is exactly the deviation flagged in Bryan's own unanswered 2026-09-18 comment about switching Category to multi-select checkboxes — except the shipped code is single-select-behaving-as-checkboxes, which is neither the AC's radio-button spec nor Bryan's own proposed multi-select. It is a third, undiscussed state.

## 3. Over-scope — every file/behaviour the ticket didn't ask for

| File/behaviour | (a) necessary plumbing / (b) unrelated | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx:149` | **(b) unrelated** | One-line comment addition (`// shippingAddress is Record<string,unknown>...`), zero logic change, zero connection to filters. Untiered file, but not in this ticket's manifest by any reading. |
| `theme/foundation/colour.ts` (+`grey[150]`), `theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (+`border-tertiary`) | **(a) necessary value, wrong process — this is the one I'd stop the loop for** | Both files are named, explicitly, in `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`'s Tier 1 list, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #3 says design-token changes go through the UI designer, full stop. The new token genuinely gets used (`zimmAccordion.css.ts:20-21`'s divider, `product-list/index.tsx:1114,1137`'s bar separator) — so I'm not saying it's decorative churn — but nothing in the commit (`c0da306d fix(filters): correct drawer layout, checkbox spacing, and grey[150] token`) or the code cites a designer sign-off, in a codebase that otherwise consistently cites "Figma-confirmed," "audited," or "PO-approved" for every other new value. This is a Tier 1 file touched without visible authorisation — a hard stop on its own, independent of everything else in this table. |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` (net -143 lines rewritten), `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` (`hasOverlay` prop) | **Mixed — real fix bundled with wide unrelated collateral** | `hasOverlay` (index.tsx) is harmless, additive, and unused beyond its own default (`product-list/index.tsx:1359` passes `true`, the default) — low-cost, arguably unneeded, not harmful. The recipe rewrite is the problem: it touches **every size variant** (`large`, `tablet`, `small`, `xLarge`, `prompt`, `mobile`), not just the `large` size the new filter drawer actually uses. `large` is also what `ZimmPdpDrawer` renders at `xl` breakpoint (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx:977-980`) — SFCC-736, status **In SIT**. `prompt` belongs to `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch` (SFCC-831, already-approved). `small` belongs to both the PDP "Find in Boutique" drawer and `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (SFCC-742, a different developer's ticket). The rewrite also **reverts** an explicitly-documented, explicitly-approved value: `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` goes from `80px` back to `72px` (`zimmDrawer.css.ts:57`), undoing a fix the deleted comment says was "approved 2026-09-12 (Wishlist/Login)" after a live Playwright re-measurement — and the new comment re-attributes the reversal to "SFCC-926 (Figma)," a ticket already merged into `develop` *before* this PR branched (confirmed: `6babac68` is an ancestor of the PR base). So a third ticket is being cited to justify undoing a second ticket's signed-off fix, from inside a first ticket's PR, for a size variant that ticket doesn't even use. That's the "different owner, different approver" collision the brief warns about, in concrete form. |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` (net +5 lines, but a real internal rewrite) | **Mixed** | Adding `ariaLabel`/`role`/`ariaChecked` to `ZimmLabelButtonProps` (lines 37, 52, 95, 105, 145, 169, 178, 181) is legitimate, minimal plumbing — `ZimmSizeFilter`'s chip buttons need it. Splitting `variant="social"` into its own `ZimmSocialButtonProps` type is a plausible side effect of that. But the *implementation* swap — replacing the recipe-driven `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmSocialButton', ...)` render with hand-rolled inline `React.CSSProperties` (commit `f7607681 fix(zimm-button): use plain span + inline style for social icon box`, no ticket cited) — has nothing to do with filters. `variant="social"` (Apple/Google sign-in) was already shipped on `develop` via SFCC-926 before this branch existed; this PR reopens and re-implements someone else's already-merged auth work. |
| `constants/index.ts` | **Mixed** | The `cssColorGroups` re-export (line ~176) is real, necessary plumbing for AC8's swatches. The full-file reformat of the unrelated `SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES` array (all 32 entries, quote/spacing/semicolon style only, no value changes) is pure autoformat noise on a checkout-country constant that has nothing to do with filters. |
| `utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts`, `utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`, `pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` | **(b) unrelated** | Each gets one identical added trailing comment (`// filterImageGroups returns a loose type; cast narrows to the SDK's typed shape`) on a pre-existing type-cast line. No behaviour change, no connection to filters — these are recently-viewed-rail/PLP-card image-selection utilities. |
| Page-level `SelectedChipRow` (CLEAR ALL + windowed chips + prev/next arrows, `product-list/index.tsx:249-316`, plus `chipsPerPage`/`chipOffset` state) | **(b) unrelated, self-admitted** | Nothing in any AC describes a page-level applied-filter chip strip with pagination arrows above the grid. The PR's own comment, `product-list/index.tsx:751-752`, says it outright: **"Applied-filter chip patterns as a page-level surface belong to SFCC-108 AC #6, not this ticket."** This is the PR building acknowledged SFCC-108 territory anyway. |

The PR description's claim of "replaces grid-fixed-width sizing on size chips with flex-wrap minimum-width" does not match what's actually shipped: `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:19` uses `<SimpleGrid columns={4}>` — a fixed grid, not flex-wrap — per that file's own comment "One flat grid of size chips using the **OOTB fixed** 44px column width." An intermediate commit (`7a0aefca`) did the opposite move ("replace custom flex... with OOTB 4-column SimpleGrid"). The PR description is describing a state the code no longer is in.

## 4. Under-scope — named items missing entirely

- **Material** — no live wiring, only the Storybook mock (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:112-120`).
- **Sleeve Length** — same, mock only (lines 122-130).
- **Availability (Available / Coming Soon)** — same, mock only (lines 105-109); no code anywhere special-cases this facet or guarantees those two exact labels.
- **Size's three named sub-groups** — the grouping *logic* exists (`zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:61-88`) but is inert against live data today, by the file's own admission (line 57: "not a front-end change").

All four are named, specific items from the current AC list. None are silently renamed or partially covered elsewhere — they are simply absent from what a shopper would see today.

## 5. Boundary bleed into SFCC-108 / SFCC-736

**Yes, in both directions, unevenly.** The `ZimmFiltersDrawerContent` organism itself is correctly scoped — it takes `content: React.ReactNode` per facet and its own docblock (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:9-14, 32-39`) is explicit that facet content is SFCC-108's job. But the actual **application wiring** in `product-list/index.tsx` does not stop at that boundary: it builds real, live-data-driven facet content itself — the Category checkbox list (lines 708-729), the colour-swatch checkbox group (lines 770-792), the size chip grid (line 771) — i.e. exactly the "radio buttons, colour swatches, size options etc." the ticket description assigns to SFCC-108. Since SFCC-108 is **Blocked**, this PR is shipping a working first draft of blocked work under cover of SFCC-847, while simultaneously not finishing the parts of that same content (Material/Sleeve/Availability/Size-grouping) that would make SFCC-108 actually closeable. The page-level chip-pagination system (§3) is the same pattern one level up, and is the one instance the PR's own comments concede outright.

I did not find any code that touches `ZimmDrawer`'s shell/overlay/slide-in/close-trigger behaviour itself (SFCC-736's actual scope) beyond the additive `hasOverlay` prop — the boundary bleed there is entirely at the CSS-recipe level described in §3, not a behavioural takeover of SFCC-736's job.

## 6. Blocker — does this depend on SFCC-104 (BM config, still Blocked)?

Partially, and the code is honest about exactly where. `grep -rn "c_categoryIds" overrides/` (searched the whole `overrides/` tree in the head worktree) returns **nothing** — Bryan's proposed new custom attribute was never actually implemented, so the shipped code does not depend on an unbuilt BM attribute for Category. Two hardcoded attribute IDs exist — `COLOR_REFINEMENT_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'c_refinementColor'` and `SIZE_REFINEMENT_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'c_size'` (`product-list/index.tsx:164,168`) — but these only route an *already-existing* refinement to a specific widget (swatch dot vs. size grid); they don't fabricate data SFCC doesn't already return. The real SFCC-104 dependency is narrower and self-documented: **Size's three sub-groups** and, most likely, **Material/Sleeve Length/Availability existing as facets at all** need BM-side refinement configuration that doesn't exist yet (`zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:57`: "Producing the grouped design is BM configuration... not a front-end change"). So: yes, part of the visible under-delivery in §4 traces directly back to the still-Blocked SFCC-104, not to missed front-end work — but that's exactly why those items should be named as open/blocked in the ticket rather than left silent.

## Required unverified-gaps section

- I did not run the app, Storybook, or a screen reader/axe pass — the WCAG line in the AC table is based on static code reading (aria attributes present in source), not a live audit.
- I did not check the actual Zimmermann Design System 2026 Figma file against any of the node-number citations in the code (e.g. `40003890:151742`, `40007982:184470`) — I'm taking those citations at face value from the comments.
- I did not check whether SFCC-104's Business Manager sandboxes currently have *any* refinement data for material/sleeve-length/availability — I'm relying on the code's own comments that this is BM-configuration-gated, not a direct BM query.
- I have not read PR #117's actual review thread/CI status (CodeRabbit findings, human approvals) beyond the ticket comment thread given to me — commit messages reference two rounds of CodeRabbit fixes already applied, but I didn't independently verify what those covered.

## What Marcel is missing

The Jira automation comment on 2026-09-16 says the story's DoR checklist failed and the issue was auto-moved back — and this PR was opened roughly an hour later, against a story Jira itself had just flagged as not ready. That sequencing (not the diff) is probably why so much of this PR reads like it's improvising scope decisions (the radio→checkbox swap, the inverted Selected-chip placement, the SFCC-108-shaped page chip strip) rather than working from a settled brief — worth checking whether the DoR gate was actually resolved before this PR is merged, independent of anything in the diff itself.</result>

This is exactly the deviation flagged in Bryan's own unanswered 2026-09-18 comment about switching Category to multi-select checkboxes — except the shipped code is single-select-behaving-as-checkboxes, which is neither the AC's radio-button spec nor Bryan's own proposed multi-select. It is a third, undiscussed state.

## 5. Boundary bleed into SFCC-108 / SFCC-736

**Yes, in both directions, unevenly.** The `ZimmFiltersDrawerContent` organism itself is correctly scoped — it takes `content: React.ReactNode` per facet and its own docblock (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:9-14, 32-39`) is explicit that facet content is SFCC-108's job. Since SFCC-108 is **Blocked**, this PR is shipping a working first draft of blocked work under cover of SFCC-847, while simultaneously not finishing the parts of that same content (Material/Sleeve/Availability/Size-grouping) that would make SFCC-108 actually closeable. The page-level chip-pagination system (§3) is the same pattern one level up, and is the one instance the PR's own comments concede outright.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

**1. Two of six new story files have no `Default` named export — components.md §Storybook > Story content: "Every story file has a `Default` named export."**

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx` — full file read (292 lines). Ten named stories (`InsideDrawer` line 202, `WithFilterTrigger` line 207, `CategoryPlpAll`, `CategoryPlpDresses`, `Selected`, `Colour`, `Size`, `Material`, `SleeveLength`, `Availability`), none named `Default`. `InsideDrawer` is the closest candidate (drawer open, nothing expanded) but isn't named `Default`. **CONFIRMED.**
- Search method: `grep -n "^export const"` per file, cross-checked by reading each file in full.
- The other four new stories files (`zimmAccordion`, `zimmCheckbox`, `zimmSelectedChip`, `zimmCheckboxGroup`) all correctly export `Default`.

### 🟡 Should-fix

**2. New `ZimmSocialButtonProps` type in `zimmButton/index.tsx` collides by name with a different component's real Props type — components.md §Components: "Props type name matches the component name."**
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx:61` declares (unexported) `type ZimmSocialButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant: 'social'; ... }` — this describes `ZimmButton`'s own `variant="social"` case, not a standalone component.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSocialButton/index.tsx:7` has a pre-existing, **exported** `export type ZimmSocialButtonProps = { icon, label, onClick, isDisabled? }` — the actual Props type of the actual `ZimmSocialButton` component.
- Confirmed this is new-in-PR, not pre-existing debt: diffed `zimmButton/index.tsx` against base — base only had `ZimmButtonBaseProps` / `ZimmLabelButtonProps` / `ZimmIconButtonProps` / `ZimmButtonProps`; `ZimmSocialButtonProps` is a `+` addition. `zimmSocialButton/index.tsx` itself is untouched by this PR (`diff -q` empty).
- Context: this looks like a deliberate in-flight consolidation — `zimmAuthDrawerContent/socialButtons.tsx` now calls `<ZimmButton variant="social">` instead of `<ZimmSocialButton>`, and grepping the whole tree for `ZimmSocialButton` (the component) turns up no remaining real caller outside its own test/story/css and one `theme/components/index.ts` registration. That consolidation itself is out of my scope to judge, but the naming collision is a components.md naming violation regardless of intent: not a TS compile error (the type is unexported/file-scoped so there's no import ambiguity), but it means the identifier `ZimmSocialButtonProps` now resolves to two unrelated shapes depending which file you're in — exactly what "Props type name matches the component name" exists to prevent. **CONFIRMED.**

**3. `ZimmSelectedChip` categorised `Commerce/` despite a fully generic props surface — components.md §Storybook > Categorisation.**
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSelectedChip/index.stories.tsx:6` → `title: 'Commerce/ZimmSelectedChip'`.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSelectedChip/index.tsx:7-16` props are `label: string; onRemove: () => void; variant?: 'primary'|'secondary'; isDisabled?: boolean` — no commerce/product/refinement type anywhere in the signature.
- Applying the table's own tiebreaker ("what does this component know about? ... nothing domain-specific → Elements/") and the Elements/ row's explicit example list, which names "Tag" as a generic-display example — this reads as a generic removable chip/tag, not a commerce-specific component like the row's own examples (ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup). Expected category: `Elements/ZimmSelectedChip`.
- Caveat: the sibling `ZimmBadge` (pre-existing, not part of this PR) is also filed under `Commerce/` despite "Badge" being an Elements/-table example — so there's an existing house tendency to file small display atoms under Commerce/ once their first real usage is commerce-flavoured, even when their own API is generic. I flag this as a judgment call, not a mechanical violation. **PLAUSIBLE.**

**4. Page-local hook location — no rule violated.** `overrides/app/pages/product-list/useFilterDrawerState.ts` lives beside its one caller rather than under `overrides/app/hooks/`. I checked both components.md's Hooks section (covers file extension, exported-name-matches-filename, typing, JSDoc — no location requirement) and conventions.md's "File naming and folder structure" section (only specifies component-folder layout under `overrides/app/components/`; says nothing about where hooks must live). `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525-529`:
```js
const handleCategoryChange = (id: string) => {
    if (id === pendingCategoryId) return;
    setPendingCategoryId(id);
    clearAll();
};
```
This only guards "clicked the same pending value twice." It never compares `id` to `categoryId` (the real, currently-applied category from the URL).

Concrete failure: shopper is on `/clothing/dresses` with `?refine=c_refinementColor=Black` already applied. They open the drawer (buffer resyncs to `pendingCategoryId="dresses"`, `pendingRefine={c_refinementColor:['Black']}`). They change their mind and click "Dresses" again → `handleCategoryChange("dresses")` → `"dresses" !== pendingCategoryId("tops")` → proceeds, `clearAll()` again (no-op, already empty). Now `pendingCategoryId === categoryId` (net category never really changed) but `pendingRefine` is still `{}`. They press APPLY → `buildAppliedRefine(searchParams.refine, managedAttributeIds, {})` (`useFilterDrawerState.ts:145-164`) deletes every managed attribute and writes nothing back → the shopper lands back on Dresses with their Black colour filter silently gone, despite never touching Colour.

`useFilterDrawerState.ts:31-36`'s own JSDoc names exactly this scenario as `resyncPendingRefine`'s reason to exist ("a caller that reverts a pending category change back to the currently-applied category... must also restore whatever refine is actually still applied"), and `useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81-95` unit-tests the function in isolation and passes. **CONFIRMED via full static trace** — every function in the chain (`handleCategoryChange`, `clearAll`, `buildAppliedRefine`) is pure and synchronous, so there's no runtime ambiguity; I did not click through a live app to watch it happen (no browser tool available to me), so treat "reproduced by execution" as not yet done. **ONE-OFF** in this PR, but the shape ("write and unit-test a fix function, forget to call it from production code, ship a green suite") is worth a broader grep if it recurs.

## likely-defect

**1. 🔴 `resyncPendingRefine` is written, unit-tested, and never wired to the one caller its own docs say needs it — applying filters after browsing categories can silently drop the shopper's other filters.**
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525-529`:
```js
const handleCategoryChange = (id: string) => {
    if (id === pendingCategoryId) return;
    setPendingCategoryId(id);
    clearAll();
};
```
This only guards "clicked the same pending value twice." It never compares `id` to `categoryId` (the real, currently-applied category from the URL).

Concrete failure: shopper is on `/clothing/dresses` with `?refine=c_refinementColor=Black` already applied. They open the drawer (buffer resyncs to `pendingCategoryId="dresses"`, `pendingRefine={c_refinementColor:['Black']}`). They click "Tops" → `handleCategoryChange("tops")` → `clearAll()` fires, `pendingRefine={}`. They change their mind and click "Dresses" again → `handleCategoryChange("dresses")` → `"dresses" !== pendingCategoryId("tops")` → proceeds, `clearAll()` again (no-op, already empty). Now `pendingCategoryId === categoryId` (net category never really changed) but `pendingRefine` is still `{}`. They press APPLY → `buildAppliedRefine(searchParams.refine, managedAttributeIds, {})` (`useFilterDrawerState.ts:145-164`) deletes every managed attribute and writes nothing back → the shopper lands back on Dresses with their Black colour filter silently gone, despite never touching Colour.

`useFilterDrawerState.ts:31-36`'s own JSDoc names exactly this scenario as `resyncPendingRefine`'s reason to exist ("a caller that reverts a pending category change back to the currently-applied category... must also restore whatever refine is actually still applied"), and `useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81-95` unit-tests the function in isolation and passes. The category chip's own `onRemove` (`index.tsx:700-703`, `setPendingCategoryId(undefined); clearAll();`) doesn't call it either, and doesn't even match the test's own inline comment ("reverting it via the category chip's onRemove") — the chip clears to `undefined`, it doesn't revert to `categoryId`. Whichever UI action the author intended as the "revert" path, it isn't wired.
**CONFIRMED via full static trace** — every function in the chain (`handleCategoryChange`, `clearAll`, `buildAppliedRefine`) is pure and synchronous, so there's no runtime ambiguity; I did not click through a live app to watch it happen (no browser tool available to me), so treat "reproduced by execution" as not yet done. **ONE-OFF** in this PR, but the shape ("write and unit-test a fix function, forget to call it from production code, ship a green suite") is worth a broader grep if it recurs.

## likely-defect

**1. 🔴 `resyncPendingRefine` is written, unit-tested, and never wired to the one caller its own docs say needs it — applying filters after browsing categories can silently drop the shopper's other filters.**
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525-529`:
```js
const handleCategoryChange = (id: string) => {
    if (id === pendingCategoryId) return;
    setPendingCategoryId(id);
    clearAll();
};
```
This only guards "clicked the same pending value twice." It never compares `id` to `categoryId` (the real, currently-applied category from the URL).

Concrete failure: shopper is on `/clothing/dresses` with `?refine=c_refinementColor=Black` already applied. They open the drawer (buffer resyncs to `pendingCategoryId="dresses"`, `pendingRefine={c_refinementColor:['Black']}`). They click "Tops" → `handleCategoryChange("tops")` → `clearAll()` fires, `pendingRefine={}`. They change their mind and click "Dresses" again → `handleCategoryChange("dresses")` → `"dresses" !== pendingCategoryId("tops")` → proceeds, `clearAll()` again (no-op, already empty). Now `pendingCategoryId === categoryId` (net category never really changed) but `pendingRefine` is still `{}`. They press APPLY → `buildAppliedRefine(searchParams.refine, managedAttributeIds, {})` (`useFilterDrawerState.ts:145-164`) deletes every managed attribute and writes nothing back → the shopper lands back on Dresses with their Black colour filter silently gone, despite never touching Colour.

`useFilterDrawerState.ts:31-36`'s own JSDoc names exactly this scenario as `resyncPendingRefine`'s reason to exist ("a caller that reverts a pending category change back to the currently-applied category... must also restore whatever refine is actually still applied"), and `useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81-95` unit-tests the function in isolation and passes. But `resyncPendingRefine` is destructured at `index.tsx:507` and never called again anywhere in the file (`grep -rn "resyncPendingRefine"` across the whole head worktree returns only the hook's own definition/JSDoc/test and this one unused destructure — confirmed, not just described). The category chip's own `onRemove` (`index.tsx:700-703`, `setPendingCategoryId(undefined); clearAll();`) doesn't call it either, and doesn't even match the test's own inline comment ("reverting it via the category chip's onRemove") — the chip clears to `undefined`, it doesn't revert to `categoryId`. Whichever UI action the author intended as the "revert" path, it isn't wired.
**CONFIRMED via full static trace** — every function in the chain (`handleCategoryChange`, `clearAll`, `buildAppliedRefine`) is pure and synchronous, so there's no runtime ambiguity; I did not click through a live app to watch it happen (no browser tool available to me), so treat "reproduced by execution" as not yet done. **ONE-OFF** in this PR, but the shape ("write and unit-test a fix function, forget to call it from production code, ship a green suite") is worth a broader grep if it recurs.

**2. 🔴 The "shop by store" filter (`StoreInventoryFilter` / `ilids`) has been dropped entirely, with no replacement and no acknowledgment anywhere in the diff.**
Base (`pr117-base/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:552-560, 717-720, 885-887`) renders `<StoreInventoryFilter toggleFilter={toggleFilter} selectedFilters={...} />` in both the desktop sidebar and the mobile filter modal, gated by `storeLocatorEnabled` (`config/default.js:44` sets this `true` by default — a genuinely live, on-by-default feature, also used by the header's store locator). Head has **zero** references to `StoreInventoryFilter`, `createStoreInventoryFilter`, or `storeLocatorEnabled` anywhere in `product-list/index.tsx` (grepped, none found) — yet `searchByInventory`/`setSearchByInventory` state (`index.tsx:360`), the `refine` computation that folds it in (`index.tsx:378`), and `applyFilters`'s careful "leave `ilids` untouched, it isn't one of this drawer's managed facets" comment (`index.tsx:624, 634`) are all still present. `setSearchByInventory` is now called from exactly one place in the whole file — `resetFilters()` setting it to `null` (`index.tsx:929`) — there is no code path left that ever sets it to a real value. The state, the refine-merge plumbing, and the defensive "don't clobber ilids" logic in `buildAppliedRefine` all still exist to serve a UI trigger that no longer exists anywhere.

Concrete failure: a shopper who could previously filter "show only items available at my local boutique" can no longer do so at all, on desktop or mobile, with no error, no fallback, and no ticket/comment anywhere in this diff acknowledging the removal (contrast with the Size sub-groups gap and the "Selected" chip variant, both of which the author explicitly flagged as pending elsewhere in this same PR).
**CONFIRMED** — direct base-vs-head diff of a real, config-enabled feature. **ONE-OFF** (specific to this migration, not a repeating pattern).

**3. 🔴 Category renders as `Checkbox`, not `RadioGroup`/`Radio` — direct AC violation, and inconsistent with every other facet type this same PR built.**
`index.tsx:710-726` renders `resolvedCategoryOptions.map(...)` as Chakra `<Checkbox isChecked={pendingCategoryId === id} onChange={() => handleCategoryChange(id)}>`. The ticket's AC is explicit: "Category - PLP (All) [all top-level category options as **RADIO BUTTONS**]" and "Category - PLP (Dresses) [... as **RADIO BUTTONS**]". `Radio`/`RadioGroup` are imported (`index.tsx:40-41`) and never used anywhere else in the file (only a stray mention inside a comment at line 1353) — confirmed via both `grep` and a real `eslint` run (`'Radio' is defined but never used` / `'RadioGroup' is defined but never used`), meaning this was scaffolded and then abandoned mid-PR, not a considered substitution. Behaviourally it *acts* single-select (the `handleCategoryChange` early-return + always-overwrite pattern prevents independent toggling), but it is announced to assistive tech as a set of independent checkboxes, not a mutually-exclusive radio group — an AT user gets no signal that picking one deselects the others. It also misses the `ADD_FILTER`/`REMOVE_FILTER` accessible-name pattern this exact PR built and applied consistently to every *other* facet control (`ZimmCheckbox`, `ZimmSizeFilter` both import and use `ADD_FILTER`/`REMOVE_FILTER` from `refinementValues.ts`; the bare Chakra `<Checkbox>` at line 711 has no `aria-label` at all beyond its child `<Text>`).
**CONFIRMED** (read + eslint output). **ONE-OFF** — the only facet still on bare Chakra primitives instead of the new atoms this PR introduced for everything else.

## likely-defect

**1. 🔴 `resyncPendingRefine` is written, unit-tested, and never wired to the one caller its own docs say needs it — applying filters after browsing categories can silently drop the shopper's other filters.**
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525-529`:
```js
const handleCategoryChange = (id: string) => {
    if (id === pendingCategoryId) return;
    setPendingCategoryId(id);
    clearAll();
};
```
This only guards "clicked the same pending value twice." It never compares `id` to `categoryId` (the real, currently-applied category from the URL).

Concrete failure: shopper is on `/clothing/dresses` with `?refine=c_refinementColor=Black` already applied. They open the drawer (buffer resyncs to `pendingCategoryId="dresses"`, `pendingRefine={c_refinementColor:['Black']}`). They click "Tops" → `handleCategoryChange("tops")` → `clearAll()` fires, `pendingRefine={}`. They change their mind and click "Dresses" again → `handleCategoryChange("dresses")` → `"dresses" !== pendingCategoryId("tops")` → proceeds, `clearAll()` again (no-op, already empty). Now `pendingCategoryId === categoryId` (net category never really changed) but `pendingRefine` is still `{}`. They press APPLY → `buildAppliedRefine(searchParams.refine, managedAttributeIds, {})` (`useFilterDrawerState.ts:145-164`) deletes every managed attribute and writes nothing back → the shopper lands back on Dresses with their Black colour filter silently gone, despite never touching Colour.

`useFilterDrawerState.ts:31-36`'s own JSDoc names exactly this scenario as `resyncPendingRefine`'s reason to exist ("a caller that reverts a pending category change back to the currently-applied category... must also restore whatever refine is actually still applied"), and `useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81-95` unit-tests the function in isolation and passes. But `resyncPendingRefine` is destructured at `index.tsx:507` and never called again anywhere in the file (`grep -rn "resyncPendingRefine"` across the whole head worktree returns only the hook's own definition/JSDoc/test and this one unused destructure — confirmed, not just described). The category chip's own `onRemove` (`index.tsx:700-703`, `setPendingCategoryId(undefined); clearAll();`) doesn't call it either, and doesn't even match the test's own inline comment ("reverting it via the category chip's onRemove") — the chip clears to `undefined`, it doesn't revert to `categoryId`. Whichever UI action the author intended as the "revert" path, it isn't wired.
**CONFIRMED via full static trace** — every function in the chain (`handleCategoryChange`, `clearAll`, `buildAppliedRefine`) is pure and synchronous, so there's no runtime ambiguity; I did not click through a live app to watch it happen (no browser tool available to me), so treat "reproduced by execution" as not yet done. **ONE-OFF** in this PR, but the shape ("write and unit-test a fix function, forget to call it from production code, ship a green suite") is worth a broader grep if it recurs.

**2. 🔴 The "shop by store" filter (`StoreInventoryFilter` / `ilids`) has been dropped entirely, with no replacement and no acknowledgment anywhere in the diff.**
Base (`pr117-base/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:552-560, 717-720, 885-887`) renders `<StoreInventoryFilter toggleFilter={toggleFilter} selectedFilters={...} />` in both the desktop sidebar and the mobile filter modal, gated by `storeLocatorEnabled` (`config/default.js:44` sets this `true` by default — a genuinely live, on-by-default feature, also used by the header's store locator). Head has **zero** references to `StoreInventoryFilter`, `createStoreInventoryFilter`, or `storeLocatorEnabled` anywhere in `product-list/index.tsx` (grepped, none found) — yet `searchByInventory`/`setSearchByInventory` state (`index.tsx:360`), the `refine` computation that folds it in (`index.tsx:378`), and `applyFilters`'s careful "leave `ilids` untouched, it isn't one of this drawer's managed facets" comment (`index.tsx:624, 634`) are all still present. `setSearchByInventory` is now called from exactly one place in the whole file — `resetFilters()` setting it to `null` (`index.tsx:929`) — there is no code path left that ever sets it to a real value. The state, the refine-merge plumbing, and the defensive "don't clobber ilids" logic in `buildAppliedRefine` all still exist to serve a UI trigger that no longer exists anywhere.

Concrete failure: a shopper who could previously filter "show only items available at my local boutique" can no longer do so at all, on desktop or mobile, with no error, no fallback, and no ticket/comment anywhere in this diff acknowledging the removal (contrast with the Size sub-groups gap and the "Selected" chip variant, both of which the author explicitly flagged as pending elsewhere in this same PR).
**CONFIRMED** — direct base-vs-head diff of a real, config-enabled feature. **ONE-OFF** (specific to this migration, not a repeating pattern).

**3. 🔴 Category renders as `Checkbox`, not `RadioGroup`/`Radio` — direct AC violation, and inconsistent with every other facet type this same PR built.**
`index.tsx:710-726` renders `resolvedCategoryOptions.map(...)` as Chakra `<Checkbox isChecked={pendingCategoryId === id} onChange={() => handleCategoryChange(id)}>`. The ticket's AC is explicit: "Category - PLP (All) [all top-level category options as **RADIO BUTTONS**]" and "Category - PLP (Dresses) [... as **RADIO BUTTONS**]". `Radio`/`RadioGroup` are imported (`index.tsx:40-41`) and never used anywhere else in the file (only a stray mention inside a comment at line 1353) — confirmed via both `grep` and a real `eslint` run (`'Radio' is defined but never used` / `'RadioGroup' is defined but never used`), meaning this was scaffolded and then abandoned mid-PR, not a considered substitution. Behaviourally it *acts* single-select (the `handleCategoryChange` early-return + always-overwrite pattern prevents independent toggling), but it is announced to assistive tech as a set of independent checkboxes, not a mutually-exclusive radio group — an AT user gets no signal that picking one deselects the others. cat >> ~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-847/review-pr117.md <<'EOF'

## FINDINGS (continued — added after browser repro + verification)
12. [in-scope defect, HIGHEST CONSEQUENCE] CONFIRMED BY LIVE BROWSER REPRO on the PR's own MRT preview — applying filters after browsing categories silently discards refinements the shopper never touched.
    Repro: GET /clothing/dresses?refine=c_refinementColor%3DBlack (chips: DRESSES, BLACK) -> open FILTERS -> expand CATEGORY -> click Tops -> click Dresses (back to the applied category) -> press APPLY.
    Result: lands on /clothing/dresses?limit=25&sort=best-matches, chips show DRESSES only. The Black colour filter is gone.
    Root cause: product-list/index.tsx:525-529 handleCategoryChange compares only against pendingCategoryId, never against the applied categoryId, and calls clearAll() on every change. useFilterDrawerState.ts:94 resyncPendingRefine exists and is unit-tested (useFilterDrawerState.test.ts:81) precisely for this case, is destructured at index.tsx:507, and is never called anywhere in overrides/ (recursive grep, head worktree). Lint independently flags it assigned-but-never-used. State: pending adjudication — this is the one I would block on.
13. [in-scope defect] CONFIRMED (recursive grep of entire overrides/ tree, both worktrees) — the store-inventory / shop-by-boutique PLP filter is gone. BASE product-list/index.tsx:74 imports StoreInventoryFilter, :270 reads storeLocatorEnabled, :552-556 createStoreInventoryFilter renders it into both sidebar and mobile modal. HEAD has no import, no storeLocatorEnabled, no render — only orphaned searchByInventory state (:360), the ilids refine merge (:378), and three comments still referencing it. storeLocatorEnabled remains live in header/_app/product-view, so the feature now exists everywhere except the PLP. Not mentioned in the ticket, ACs, PR description, or any commit message. State: pending adjudication.
14. [in-scope defect] CONFIRMED (grep both worktrees) — no aria-live/status region anywhere in the new work (16 files at base, 16 at head, zero in any PR-touched file). Fails SFCC-847's WCAG a11y AC (SC 4.1.3 Status Messages): APPLY, chip removal and chip pagination all change results with no non-visual signal. NOTE ON FAIRNESS: the "accessible filter announcements" line is in CodeRabbit's auto-generated summary, not the author's own description — do not characterise this as the author overclaiming.
15. [in-scope defect] CONFIRMED (live API capture + source) — empty facets are rendered as clickable accordions that expand to nothing. SFCC returns c_colourFilter "Colour Filter" valueCount 0, c_materialFilter "Material" valueCount 0, c_outOfStockStatus "Availability" valueCount 0 on /clothing/dresses. product-list/index.tsx:738-740 maps every returned refinement into an accordion with no values.length guard. Same three empty accordions confirmed on /clothing/tops, /accessories/bags, /clothing. FAIRNESS: the empty data is SFCC-104's (Blocked); the missing guard is this PR's. One-line fix.
16. [not a defect — checked and cleared] Zero-hit filtering is correct. API returns c_size 56 values of which 46 have hitCount 0 -> 10 render; c_refinementColor 18 values of which 3 have hitCount 0 (Red, Purple, Grey) -> 15 render. Both correct. Did not file.
17. [tool artifact — discarded, do not report] My cross-breakpoint script reported drawer panel widths of 729/971/1367px. That was my own selector grabbing the first [role=dialog] including a hidden one. The correctly-filtered measurement is 720x1024 at x=720 on a 1440 viewport, which matches Figma exactly. Discarded.
18. [needs Marcel] PLAUSIBLE — CLEAR ALL measures 0x0 below 768px and 60.5x26 at 768px+. Either it is intentionally desktop-only or it is missing on mobile. Not yet settled.
EOF
echo "appended"

**After (head, `zimmButton/index.tsx`, inline `style` object on a plain `<span>`):**

## 2. `variant="social"` icon regression — exact CSS and predicted rendered consequence

**Before (base, `zimmSocialButton.css.ts` `icon` part, applied via `useMultiStyleConfig`):**
```js
icon: {
  display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', flexShrink: 0,
  '& svg': { width: '100%', height: '100%' },   // ← forces the SVG to fill the box
},
// + size-keyed: sizes.md.icon = { width: 'var(--zimm-icon-size-md)', height: 'var(--zimm-icon-size-md)' }  // 16px
```

**After (head, `zimmButton/index.tsx`, inline `style` object on a plain `<span>`):**
```js
const iconBoxStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', flexShrink: 0,
  width: `var(--zimm-icon-size-${iconSizeToken})`,   // still 16px on the box itself
  height: `var(--zimm-icon-size-${iconSizeToken})`,
  ...props.iconSx,
};
// no '& svg' rule — and a React inline `style` object structurally cannot express one;
// this isn't a value that got dropped, it's a capability the new mechanism doesn't have
```

**Mechanism:** `ZimmAppleSignInIcon`/`ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` (`overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:484,495`, confirmed by direct read) are Chakra `createIcon({viewBox:'0 0 16 16', ...})` with no explicit `boxSize` override — Chakra's `Icon` defaults that to `1em × 1em`, i.e. font-relative. With the `'& svg'` rule gone, the rendered `<svg>` sizes itself off the **inherited font-size**, which for `size="social"` (`zimmButton.css.ts:296,302`, values confirmed from that file's own comments) is `var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)` = **12px** below `md`, stepping to `var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)` = **14px** at `md`+.

**Predicted, falsifiable consequence:**
- **Shrinks — does not distort.** Both width and height scale off the same `1em`, so the 16×16 viewBox's aspect ratio (1:1) is preserved; this is a uniform shrink, not a stretch/squash.
- **Magnitude: renders at 12px on mobile (75% of the intended 16px, a 25% reduction), 14px at ≥md (87.5% of intended, a 12.5% reduction)** — versus a constant 16px at base regardless of viewport.
- **The outer box does NOT shrink** — the wrapping `<span>` still gets explicit `width/height: var(--zimm-icon-size-md)` (16px) from `iconBoxStyle` itself; only the `<svg>` inside is undersized. Net visible effect: the Apple/Google glyph appears to float with a faint ring of empty space inside its slot rather than filling it edge-to-edge, and is very slightly larger at desktop than mobile — where base rendered a constant 16px everywhere.
- **How to kill or confirm it:** inspect the `<svg>` inside `socialButtons.tsx`'s rendered Apple/Google button at a real phone-width viewport and again at ≥768px — `getBoundingClientRect()` or computed `width`/`height` should read **~12px then ~14px** at head if this is real, versus a fixed 16px if it isn't (e.g. if I'm wrong about `createIcon`'s default `boxSize`, or something else in the cascade sets `font-size` on the span/svg itself that I haven't seen).

## 2. `variant="social"` icon regression — exact CSS and predicted rendered consequence

**Before (base, `zimmSocialButton.css.ts` `icon` part, applied via `useMultiStyleConfig`):**
```js
icon: {
  display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', flexShrink: 0,
  '& svg': { width: '100%', height: '100%' },   // ← forces the SVG to fill the box
},
// + size-keyed: sizes.md.icon = { width: 'var(--zimm-icon-size-md)', height: 'var(--zimm-icon-size-md)' }  // 16px
```

**After (head, `zimmButton/index.tsx`, inline `style` object on a plain `<span>`):**
```js
const iconBoxStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', flexShrink: 0,
  width: `var(--zimm-icon-size-${iconSizeToken})`,   // still 16px on the box itself
  height: `var(--zimm-icon-size-${iconSizeToken})`,
  ...props.iconSx,
};
// no '& svg' rule — and a React inline `style` object structurally cannot express one;
// this isn't a value that got dropped, it's a capability the new mechanism doesn't have
```

**Mechanism:** `ZimmAppleSignInIcon`/`ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` (`overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:484,495`, confirmed by direct read) are Chakra `createIcon({viewBox:'0 0 16 16', ...})` with no explicit `boxSize` override — Chakra's `Icon` defaults that to `1em × 1em`, i.e. font-relative. With the `'& svg'` rule gone, the rendered `<svg>` sizes itself off the **inherited font-size**, which for `size="social"` (`zimmButton.css.ts:296,302`, values confirmed from that file's own comments) is `var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)` = **12px** below `md`, stepping to `var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)` = **14px** at `md`+.

**Predicted, falsifiable consequence:**
- **Shrinks — does not distort.** Both width and height scale off the same `1em`, so the 16×16 viewBox's aspect ratio (1:1) is preserved; this is a uniform shrink, not a stretch/squash.
- **Magnitude: renders at 12px on mobile (75% of the intended 16px, a 25% reduction), 14px at ≥md (87.5% of intended, a 12.5% reduction)** — versus a constant 16px at base regardless of viewport.
- **The outer box does NOT shrink** — the wrapping `<span>` still gets explicit `width/height: var(--zimm-icon-size-md)` (16px) from `iconBoxStyle` itself; only the `<svg>` inside is undersized. Net visible effect: the Apple/Google glyph appears to float with a faint ring of empty space inside its slot rather than filling it edge-to-edge, and is very slightly larger at desktop than mobile — where base rendered a constant 16px everywhere.
- **How to kill or confirm it:** inspect the `<svg>` inside `socialButtons.tsx`'s rendered Apple/Google button at a real phone-width viewport and again at ≥768px — `getBoundingClientRect()` or computed `width`/`height` should read **~12px then ~14px** at head if this is real, versus a fixed 16px if it isn't (e.g. if I'm wrong about `createIcon`'s default `boxSize`, or something else in the cascade sets `font-size` on the span/svg itself that I haven't seen).

content.text:
# PR #117 — SFCC-847 filter drawer (author: Bryan De Vera)

**State right now:** OPEN · head `464c6801` · **mergeable: CONFLICTING** · no human approval yet. CodeRabbit approved it last night after five rounds. Develop has moved 8 commits past this PR's base, so it can't merge as-is regardless of what we decide.

## 1. Gates — head vs base

| Gate | Base `5f50a39e` | Head `464c6801` | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | no change |
| `npm run test` | 105 files / 1536 tests | 113 files / **1594** tests, all pass | +58 tests, genuinely better |
| `npm run lint` *(not CI-gated here)* | 1170 problems | 1189 problems | +19. Net of `constants/index.ts` improving by 34 and `product-list/index.tsx` worsening by 32 |
| `audit:tokens` | 6 unacknowledged | 6 unacknowledged | no regression — his new raw values are correctly annotated |

**CI checks that actually ran:** unit tests, Storybook a11y, deploy preview, branch target, file tier. **Skipped:** Playwright E2E and BrowserStack. Both skips are legitimate under the change-scoping rules, but it means nothing exercised this feature end to end before I did.

## 2. Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore

**1 · A shopper loses filters they never touched. CONFIRMED — I reproduced it in a browser on his own preview.**
Land on Dresses with a Black colour filter on. Open Filters, expand Category, click Tops, change your mind, click Dresses again, press Apply. You land back on Dresses with **Black silently gone**.
Why: `handleCategoryChange` ([product-list/index.tsx:525](overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:525)) only checks whether you clicked the same *pending* value twice — never whether you've landed back on the category that was already applied — and wipes the buffer on every change. He wrote the function that fixes exactly this, `resyncPendingRefine`, and unit-tested it. It's destructured at line 507 and **never called anywhere in `overrides/`**. Lint flags it as unused.

**2 · The "shop by boutique" filter has disappeared from the PLP. CONFIRMED.**
Base imports and renders `StoreInventoryFilter` into both the sidebar and the mobile modal. Head has no import, no render, no `storeLocatorEnabled` — but keeps the `searchByInventory` state, the `ilids` merge, and three comments still talking about it. The feature is still live in the header, PDP and `_app`, so it now exists everywhere *except* the page it filters. Not mentioned in the ticket, the ACs, the PR description, or any commit message.

**3 · Three accordions expand to nothing, on every PLP. CONFIRMED live.**
COLOUR FILTER, MATERIAL and AVAILABILITY all open to an empty panel — same on `/clothing/dresses`, `/clothing/tops`, `/accessories/bags`, `/clothing`. And COLOR plus COLOUR FILTER both render as separate facets.
I pulled the API response: SFCC returns those three with **zero values**. [product-list/index.tsx:738](overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:738) maps every returned refinement into an accordion with no check that it has any values. **Be fair to him here** — the empty data is SFCC-104's problem and that ticket is Blocked. The missing guard is his, and it's one line.

**4 · A drawer height fix from someone else's ticket got reverted, and its rationale deleted. CONFIRMED three independent ways.**
`HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` goes 80px → 72px in the shared drawer recipe. The ~22-line comment explaining that 80px came from live Playwright measurement and was "a deliberate cross-consumer widening approved 2026-09-12 (Wishlist/Login)" is gone, along with two more rationale blocks. Three real consumers get the mobile header: this new drawer, the Wishlist/Login drawer on actual phones, and the country/language prompt. No test asserts the value, so the green suite can't see it.
AGENTS.md says don't remove comments unless you're removing the code they describe — the constant stayed, only its value changed.

**5 · No screen-reader announcement anywhere in the new work. CONFIRMED.**
Zero `aria-live` in any file this PR touched. Apply, chip removal and chip paging all change the results with no non-visual signal — that's the WCAG accessibility AC on the ticket. One fairness note: the "accessible filter announcements" line is in CodeRabbit's auto-generated blurb, not his description, so this is a gap, not an overclaim.

**6 · Category ships checkboxes; the ACs say radio buttons. CONFIRMED.**
It behaves single-select but announces as independent checkboxes, so a screen-reader user gets no signal that picking one deselects the last. `Radio` and `RadioGroup` are imported and never used — he started down the radio path and switched.

**7 · Two of six new story files have no `Default` export** — `zimmSizeFilter` and `zimmFiltersDrawerContent`. components.md requires one in every story file.

**8 · Shared drawer constant de-shared, and the copies have already drifted.** `NARROW_WIDTH_ABOVE_MD` existed specifically "so the width/floor/cap triple can't drift." It's gone; the values are hand-typed in two places, and `prompt` has already lost its `maxWidth` and re-types `'25%'` raw.

**9 · Size renders as a flat list, not the three groups the ACs specify.** Root cause is Business Manager config (SFCC-104, Blocked), not his code. His own comment says so. This should be named as blocked, not fixed here.

**10 · PR body is essentially the unfilled template** — no description, ticket field left as "SFCC-", "(change 1)", "(step 1)", all tier checkboxes unticked.

## 3. What I checked and **dropped** — this matters as much as the list above

- **Social sign-in icons "will shrink to 12px".** Two agents reached this independently from the source. I measured it in the browser: **24×24 at both 390px and 1440px**, with a 14px button font. If it were font-relative it would be 14px. Dead.
- **"CLEAR ALL missing on mobile."** My own selector artifact — it's there, 60.5×26 at 390px.
- **"Tier 1 files touched without approval."** He *is* in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (verified live), and commit `c0da306d` documents it in AGENTS.md's exact prescribed wording. CODEOWNERS auto-requested the Tier-1 team. **He followed the process correctly** — only the template checkbox is unticked. I'm not posting this as a violation.
- **"Material/Sleeve Length/Availability not delivered."** Wrong — all three render; Sleeve Length works perfectly with live data.
- **My own drawer widths at 768/1024/1440.** Selector artifact; the real measurement is 720×1024 at x=720, an exact Figma match.

## 4. Scope verdict: **both over and under**

Under on the ACs (empty facets, flat sizes, checkbox-not-radio, no announcements). Over on everything else — the page-level chip strip (his own code comment says it "belong[s] to SFCC-108 AC #6, not this ticket"), the shared drawer recipe rewrite, a one-line comment in a **checkout** file (Squad A, while this is labelled Squad B), and a 33-entry reformat of the shipping-country constants.

Design fidelity where it *is* implemented is genuinely good: drawer 720×1024 at x=720, 64px accordion rows with 20/24/20 padding, 52px Clear/Apply — all exact Figma matches.

## 5. What nobody verified

- No screen reader was run. The aria findings are from source and DOM, not VoiceOver.
- Focus behaviour when an accordion collapses under a focused control is traced through Chakra's source but not reproduced.
- I reviewed the diff as it stands; it conflicts with develop, so **what finally merges may not be what I reviewed**.
- Only one Figma state exists to check against (see below).
- A verification pass on the secondary findings (7, 8, and the checkbox target-size arithmetic) is still running.

## 6. What Marcel is missing

- **The Figma trail for this story is broken.** Kiera's "Designs are done" comment links `Zimmermann_Designs` node `3216-7913` — that node is **"Footer SEO Expand"**, not the filter drawer. The only usable spec I found is Design System node `40003890-151730`, which is the collapsed desktop state *only*. There is no node for expanded facets, the Selected variant, or any mobile state. Anyone building or reviewing against this ticket is working blind on most of it.
- **SFCC-847 is still "In Progress" and failed its own Definition of Ready.** Jira auto-bounced it on 16 Sep for incomplete DoR; the PR was opened about an hour later.
- **The ACs were never cleaned up.** Bianca committed on 9 Sep to move the facet-content ACs to SFCC-108. They're still on SFCC-847, so the description and the ACs now contradict each other — which is part of why this PR's scope is ambiguous.
- **Bryan's 18 Sep `c_categoryIds` proposal got no reply from anyone.** He proposed a new backend attribute and a switch to multi-select. Nobody answered, and he correctly didn't build it — but that's an open architecture question sitting unanswered in a ticket that's about to merge.
- **`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is lying to every session.** It describes `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as live in `zimmButton.css.ts`. They exist nowhere in `overrides/` and haven't for a while. Pre-dates this PR, but it's Tier 1 and loaded into every context.
- **CodeRabbit approved this after finding one i18n nit.** It caught none of the six real defects. Worth knowing before anyone treats its green tick as coverage.

Findings are written to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-847/review-pr117.md`. **Nothing is posted to GitHub.**

questions.question: On the top two — silent filter loss on Apply, and the store-inventory filter disappearing from the PLP — what's the verdict?

options.label: Request changes on both
options.description: Both are shopper-facing regressions on a PR with no E2E coverage. Post as blocking, with the browser repro steps for the filter-loss one so he can reproduce it himself.

options.label: Request changes on filter loss only
options.description: Block on the filter-loss bug. Raise the store-inventory removal as a question about intent — he may have descoped it deliberately and just not said so.

options.label: Comment-only on both
options.description: Raise both as questions rather than a block, given the PR already can't merge on conflicts and he's a tier-1-approver peer.

options.label: Hold everything until he rebases
options.description: The diff conflicts with develop. Say nothing yet, re-review after the rebase, avoid commenting on code that may change.

questions.question: The shared drawer recipe change reverts an approved 80px header fix from SFCC-742's territory and deletes ~30 lines of rationale. How do you want that handled?

options.label: Ask him to lift it out of this PR
options.description: The whole zimmDrawer.css.ts rewrite touches three consumers across two other tickets. Ask for it as its own PR so the Wishlist/Login owner can review the revert on its merits.

options.label: Ask only to restore the value and comments
options.description: Narrower ask: put HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE back to 80px and restore the deleted rationale blocks, leave the rest of the recipe work in place.

options.label: Flag the conflict, let him choose
options.description: Post the evidence that 80px was measured and approved under a different ticket on 2026-09-12, cite the AGENTS.md comment rule, and ask which way he wants to resolve it.

options.label: Take it to the SFCC-742 owner first

<result>## PR #117 — TypeScript Idiom Compliance Audit

Scope: `.claude/rules/typescript.md`, all 33 changed files. Read-only; no fixes applied. `tsc`/lint findings below were verified by actually running them against the head worktree, not assumed.

### Checks 1–4 and 9 — summary (clean, with two corrections to the task's framing)

- **`any` (#1):** Zero new `any` introduced. All 6 `any` sites live in `pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` (lines 19, 70, 72, 129, 144, 198) and are byte-identical in the base worktree — this PR's only touch to that file is adding a justifying comment to an unrelated `as string | undefined` cast at line 149. Not a PR #117 issue.
- **Non-null assertions (#2):** Ran ESLint directly — confirms exactly 4 `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion` hits, all in `pages/product-list/index.tsx` (lines 847, 892 ×2 nested, 900). **All 4 are pre-existing**, confirmed byte-identical at base-worktree lines 396/441/443/449. A whole-diff regex sweep (`grep -P '^\+.*[A-Za-z0-9_\)\]]!(?!=)'` across all 4255 diff lines) confirms **zero non-null assertions were added anywhere in this PR**. The task's framing implied these might be new — they are not.
- **`type` vs `interface` (#3):** Zero `interface` declarations anywhere in the 33 files, old or new. Nothing to flag.
- **`import type` (#4):** Checked every import line added by the PR (~50 across all files). All type-only imports correctly use `import type` or an inline `type` specifier (e.g. `zimmButton/index.tsx:2`, `:4`). No violations.
- **Generic naming (#9):** No new generic type parameters introduced anywhere in the diff — nothing to check.

### Check 5 — Discriminated union (the main event)

**Condensed type definitions, `zimmButton/index.tsx`:**
```ts
type ZimmButtonBaseProps = { label: string; type?: ...; disabled?: boolean; ariaDisabled?: boolean;
  inverse?: boolean; onClick?: () => void; style?: CSSProperties; sx?: SystemStyleObject; ariaLabel?: string; };

type ZimmLabelButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & {
  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'; size?: 'large'|'medium'|'adaptive'; fullWidth?: boolean;
  ariaDescribedBy?: string; iconLeading?: React.ReactNode; iconTrailing?: React.ReactNode;
} & ({ role?: never; ariaChecked?: never } | { role: 'checkbox' | 'radio'; ariaChecked: boolean });  // line 52

type ZimmIconButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant: 'icon'; icon: ZimmIconType; size?: ZimmIconSize; };

type ZimmSocialButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant: 'social'; icon: React.ReactNode;
  iconSize?: ZimmIconSize; iconSx?: React.CSSProperties; fullWidth?: boolean; };  // lines 61-75, new in this PR

export type ZimmButtonProps = ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps | ZimmSocialButtonProps;  // line 77
```

**Is it a real discriminated union?** Yes — verified empirically, not by reading alone. I wrote a scratch `.tsx` importing the real `ZimmButtonProps` and ran the project's own `npx tsc --noEmit` against 7 prop combinations (file deleted immediately after, worktree confirmed clean):

| Test | Combination | `tsc` result |
|---|---|---|
| A | `{label, role:'checkbox'}` — no `ariaChecked` | **ERROR** TS2322 |
| B | `{label, ariaChecked:true}` — no `role` | **ERROR** TS2322 |
| C | `{label, variant:'icon', icon, role:'checkbox', ariaChecked:true}` | **ERROR** TS2353 "'role' does not exist in type 'ZimmIconButtonProps'" |
| D | `{label, variant:'social', icon, role:'checkbox', ariaChecked:true}` | **ERROR** TS2353 "'role' does not exist in type 'ZimmSocialButtonProps'" |
| E | `{label, role:'tab'}` (invalid literal) | **ERROR** TS2322 |
| F | `{label, variant:'secondary', role:'checkbox', ariaChecked:true}` | no error (valid) |
| G | `{label, variant:'primary'}` | no error (valid) |

So the PR body's claim holds up: `role`/`aria-checked` genuinely cannot be declared apart, and — because `variant` is a real discriminant across all three outer-union arms — they also can't leak onto `icon`/`social` variants (C/D). This is a bit more precisely an "exclusion via `never`" pattern than a classic tagged `kind` field, but it's the correct, working idiom, not a "pile of optional fields."

**Two real gaps found, both worth flagging:**

1. **🟡 Garbled comment, `zimmButton/index.tsx:52` (CONFIRMED, new to this PR).** The 540-character line carries 5 separate `//` fragments concatenated in scrambled order (verified at byte level, not a Read-tool artifact):
   > `// \`aria-checked\` is a selectable control that never exposes what it is set to. // union so the role and its state cannot be supplied apart: a \`role="checkbox"\` with no // button and never conveys whether it is currently applied. Modelled as a discriminated // — e.g. a filter chip. Without these a screen reader announces the control as a plain // Toggle semantics, for a button that represents a *selectable state* rather than an action`

   Reversing the fragments produces coherent prose ("Toggle semantics, for a button that represents a *selectable state* rather than an action — e.g. a filter chip. Without these a screen reader announces the control as a plain button and never conveys whether it is currently applied. Modelled as a discriminated union so the role and its state cannot be supplied apart: a `role="checkbox"` with no `aria-checked` is a selectable control that never exposes what it is set to."), confirming this is a mechanical mangling (likely a Prettier collapse or bad merge), not intentional. Doesn't affect type safety, but the PR's flagship idiom ships with its own rationale unreadable at the point of use.

2. **🟡 PR body overstates actual usage.** Repo-wide grep for `role="checkbox"` (not just the 33 listed files) turns up exactly **one** real consumer: `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:31-32` (`role="checkbox" ariaChecked={isSelected}`, inside `SizeChipRow`). `zimmCheckbox/index.tsx` — the actual "checkbox refinements" component — does **not** use `ZimmButton` at all; it wraps Chakra's native `<Checkbox>`, which gets its ARIA semantics from a real `<input type="checkbox">` and never touches this discriminated union. `zimmCheckboxGroup/index.tsx` composes `ZimmCheckbox`, not `ZimmButton`, so it doesn't touch it either. The claim "used by size and checkbox refinements" is true only for size.

Minor, non-blocking observation: `variant` is optional on `ZimmLabelButtonProps` but required on the other two arms — a slight discriminant asymmetry — but tests A–G above show it discriminates correctly regardless, so not a real defect.

### Check 6 — Utility types

🟡 **CONFIRMED, new to this PR.** `zimmCheckboxGroup/index.tsx:5-12`:
```ts
export type ZimmCheckboxGroupOption = { value: string; label: string; hitCount?: number; swatchColour?: string; };
```
hand-duplicates 4 fields **verbatim, including identical JSDoc comments**, from `zimmCheckbox/index.tsx:6-15`'s `ZimmCheckboxProps` (same fields plus `isChecked`/`onChange`). Both files are 100%-new in this PR (confirmed via diff headers: `new file mode 100644`). This is textbook `Omit<ZimmCheckboxProps, 'isChecked' | 'onChange'>` — and the PR's own `zimmCheckbox/index.stories.tsx:12` uses exactly that idiom (`Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmCheckbox>, 'isChecked' | 'onChange'>`) one file away, so the pattern wasn't unfamiliar, just inconsistently applied. Low practical drift risk (both types are co-designed/new), but a clear rule violation.

Everything else clean: `productListCardMapper.ts:238` already uses `Pick<ProductListCardResult, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'>` correctly (pre-existing, untouched by this PR beyond nearby comment additions).

### Check 7 — `satisfies` vs `as`

Fully compliant. This PR's entire touch to `payment.tsx`, `productListCardMapper.ts`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` **is** adding justifying comments to 7 pre-existing casts — verified each is substantive, not a placeholder:
- `payment.tsx:149` — `// shippingAddress is Record<string,unknown>; countryCode is always a string when present`
- `productListCardMapper.ts:125,131` — `// filterImageGroups returns ProductSearchHit's loose imageGroups type; cast narrows to the SDK's typed shape` / `// same loose→typed cast as above`
- `recentlyViewedCard.ts:171,179` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:245,253` — equivalent wording for `ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]`

All 7 are narrowing casts from a loosely-typed SDK/base-package return value — exactly the case where `as` (not `satisfies`) is the right tool per typescript.md's own guidance. No violations.

### Check 8 — `readonly`

All 5 claimed additions spot-checked and CONFIRMED present in head: `zimmAccordion/index.tsx:41` (`items: readonly ZimmAccordionItem[]`), `zimmCheckboxGroup/index.tsx:15-16` (`options`/`selectedValues`), `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:11` (`selectedFilters`), `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:18` (`facetGroups`). ("`zimmSizeRefinements`" isn't a separate file — it's a comment reference to base SFCC's own `SizeRefinements.jsx`.)

### One related, out-of-scope-but-worth-a-line observation

New code in `pages/product-list/index.tsx` (`parentCategoryPath`, entirely new — zero hits in base worktree) feeds ~8 new template literals through base SFCC's untyped `useSearchParams().stringify`, each flagged by ESLint's `@typescript-eslint/restrict-template-expressions` ("Invalid type any"). This is very likely the real source of the reported +19 lint delta — not the 4 non-null assertions, which are pre-existing and lint-neutral. Not a `no-explicit-any` violation (different rule, doesn't match the literal `: any`/`as any`/`<any>` grep) and not fixable without typing an upstream untyped base-package hook, which ~6 pre-existing call sites in the same file already leave untyped — flagging for completeness, not as a rule violation.</result>
