<result>## Findings — PR #117 (SFCC-847 filter drawer)

Worktrees used: head = `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/7cadc18c-ced6-49dd-b184-e0718042bef8/scratchpad/pr117-head`, base = same path with `pr117-base`. I re-ran the gates I leaned on myself rather than trusting the supplied numbers: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean at head (reproduced), a scoped `eslint` pass on `product-list/index.tsx` at both base and head (reproduced), and a live `node` execution of the installed `query-string` package against the base SFCC parser's actual logic (reproduced, not just read).

**1. ZimmButton social-icon sizing regression — CONFIRMED.**
Diff confirms the move: base's social branch used `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmSocialButton', ...)` + `<chakra.span __css={socialStyles.icon}>`; head (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx:125-152`) replaced it with a plain `<span style={iconBoxStyle}>` — a literal DOM `style` attribute, which cannot express a `'& svg'` descendant rule. The recipe itself (`zimmSocialButton/zimmSocialButton.css.ts`) still exists, still registered, and still carries `'& svg': {width:'100%',height:'100%'}` — but nothing calls it from the new path. `ZimmAppleSignInIcon`/`ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` (`icons/zimm.tsx:484,495`) are plain `createIcon()` outputs; I read `@chakra-ui/icon`'s actual `Icon` source (`chunk-DKFDJSXF.mjs`) — default `w:'1em', h:'1em'`, no override registered for `"Icon"` in this theme. The social button's own font-size is `var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)`/`2xs` (12px/14px, `zimmButton.css.ts:296,302`), so the icon will now render at 12–14px instead of the fixed 16px box. `socialButtons.tsx` (identical at base/head) is the real production caller. Sub-claim confirmed: every social-variant test in `zimmButton/index.test.tsx:105-172` passes `icon={<span>...</span>}`, never a real SVG, and none assert on the SVG's own size.

**2. Checkbox row height / WCAG 2.5.8 Spacing exception — CONFIRMED.**
`ZimmCheckbox` (`zimmCheckbox/index.tsx`) passes no `size`, so Chakra's checkbox `defaultProps.size:'md'` applies; its `control` box resolves to `sizes.4` = `1rem` (16px) — verified in `@chakra-ui/theme`'s `chunk-3XG4KRSA.mjs` and `chunk-G3IFUAY5.mjs`, and confirmed this project does **not** override `theme.sizes` (`theme/index.ts:39`'s own comment: "sizes Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px"). `textStyle="navigation"` is `fontSize: fontSizes['3xs']` = 12px, `lineHeight:'normal'` (`typography.ts:213-219`, `checkbox.mjs` foundation `3xs=0.75rem`). `ZimmCheckboxGroup`'s `<Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-m)">` = 16px (`spacing.ts:13`), and I read Chakra's actual `Stack` source (`@chakra-ui/layout/dist/chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) — this version applies `spacing` as flex `gap`, an edge-to-edge value, not per-child margin. So: row height ≈16px (floor set by the fixed 16px control), 16px edge-to-edge gap → center-to-center ≈32px. A 24px-diameter-circle Spacing-exception test needs ≥24px separation; 32px clears it. This holds even at the pessimistic end of the row-height estimate (a taller label line-box would only widen the margin further).

**3. Accordion focus-stranding — CONFIRMED.**
Read `@chakra-ui/accordion`'s `AccordionPanel` (`chunk-WA4Q3J7T.mjs`): `if (!reduceMotion) { delete panelProps.hidden; }`, then wraps in `Collapse`. `ZimmAccordion` (`zimmAccordion/index.tsx`) never passes `reduceMotion`. Read `@chakra-ui/transition`'s `Collapse` (`chunk-LRMLOJAR.mjs`): `transitionEnd.exit` sets `display: hasStartingHeight ? 'block' : 'none'` — applied only when the exit animation *finishes*, confirming the mechanism exactly as claimed. `grep -n "\.focus("` returns nothing in `zimmAccordion/index.tsx`, `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx`, or `product-list/index.tsx`. I additionally checked Chakra's own accordion hook (`chunk-JDQBKIKM.mjs:97-116`) for a mitigating mechanism: its only `.focus()` calls live inside `onKeyDown`'s Arrow/Home/End handlers — `onClick` (line ~94) never calls `.focus()`. On the focus-trap question: I traced `react-focus-lock`'s real `activateTrap()` (`Trap.js`) — it only forcibly reclaims focus on `persistentFocus`, a window-level blur/refocus cycle, or first-mount `autoFocus`; none apply here, and it explicitly treats `document.activeElement === document.body` as "free focus" it doesn't fight. `ModalFocusScope` (`@chakra-ui/modal/chunk-LBED2F7B.mjs`) passes no `persistentFocus` to `FocusLock`. So the drawer's trap does **not** catch this — focus reverts to `body`, uncaught.

**4. Missing aria-hidden on accordion chevrons — CONFIRMED.**
`zimmAccordion/index.tsx:82-86`: `<ChevronUpIcon .../>` / `<ChevronDownIcon .../>` carry no `aria-hidden`. `zimmSelectedChip/index.tsx` (bottom): `<ZimmIcon type="close" size="md" aria-hidden={true} />` with an explicit "Decorative" comment. `zimmButton/index.tsx`: `aria-hidden={true}` on the icon-variant `ZimmIcon`, on `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` spans, and `aria-hidden="true"` on the social icon span. `icons/zimm.tsx:102-124` shows `ChevronDownIcon`/`ChevronUpIcon` are bare `createIcon()` calls with no `defaultProps`; Chakra's `Icon` source has no default `aria-hidden` anywhere.

**5. Divergent pipe-parsing, empty-value guard — CONFIRMED.**
`useFilterDrawerState.ts:54-55` guards `values[0] !== ''`. `product-list/index.tsx:994-1014`'s chip-building loop has no such guard. I didn't just reason about reachability — I executed the real installed `query-string` package against the exact logic in the base SFCC `use-search-params.js`: parsing `refine=colour=` produces `nested.colour === ''` (a bare string). That value reaches `product-list/index.tsx`'s unguarded branch and produces a chip with an empty label. Reachability caveat: I traced `buildAppliedRefine`/`setValues` and found every app-generated navigation path deletes an emptied attribute rather than setting it to `''` — so this is reachable via a hand-typed or malformed URL (`?refine=colour=`), not via any in-app click path I could find.

**6. category-links.tsx is dead code — CONFIRMED**, search scope: full-text, case-insensitive grep for `CategoryLinks`/`category-links` across the entire head worktree excluding `node_modules` and `.git`. Two hits, both inside the file's own folder (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/partials/category-links.tsx` and its `.test.tsx`). Stronger than the claim states: `product-list/index.tsx` **did** import and render `<CategoryLinks>` twice at base (`index.tsx:68,717,884`); this PR is what removed both call sites, orphaning the file.

**7. constants/index.ts reformatting + redundant export — CONFIRMED, both halves.**
Extracted `SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES` programmatically from both files (33 entries each) — value+order array is byte-identical (`JSON.stringify` equal); the diff is exclusively brace-spacing/semicolon Prettier formatting. `cssColorGroups` was added to the explicit named re-export block (head line 173) that already sits directly above a pre-existing `export * from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants';`. Confirmed `cssColorGroups` is a genuine top-level `export const` in that target module (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:71`), with no local `cssColorGroups` declared anywhere else in the override file to justify an explicit form — and `tsc --noEmit` stays clean with both present, which I re-ran myself.

**8. Pre-existing lint findings, not introduced — CONFIRMED.**
I ran `pwa-kit-dev lint` on `product-list/index.tsx` myself at both worktrees rather than trust the given totals. Head: 4 `no-non-null-assertion` warnings (847:35, 892:20 ×2, 900:35) plus unused `addItemToWishlist`(835)/`removeItemFromWishlist`(886). Base: identical shape at 396/441×2/449 and 384/435. Extracted the two code blocks (base 384-452, head 835-903) and diffed them directly — 69 lines, byte-identical. The whole region shifted ~451 lines down from unrelated insertions earlier in the file; the region itself was never touched.

**9. Fake facet placeholders in Storybook, no play functions — CONFIRMED.**
`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx` builds every facet's `content` from raw `☐`/`○` glyphs in `chakra.li`/`chakra.ul` (lines ~26-125), with its own comment block admitting this is a stand-in. Grepped the file for `ZimmCheckboxGroup`/`ZimmSizeFilter`/`ZimmSelectedChip`/`ZimmCheckbox` — zero matches — while `product-list/index.tsx:76,79,80,771,777` composes exactly those three/four as the real facet UI. Grepped all four named story files (`zimmCheckbox`, `zimmSelectedChip`, `zimmSizeFilter`, `zimmCheckboxGroup`) for the word `play` — zero occurrences in any of them.

**10. alwaysVisibleContent shows on collapse, not on expand — CONFIRMED, with one caveat.**
`zimmAccordion/index.tsx:88-91`: `{!isExpanded && item.alwaysVisibleContent && (...)}` immediately followed by `<AccordionPanel>{item.content}</AccordionPanel>` — the chip summary shows only when collapsed, the option list only when expanded (per the same Collapse mechanism confirmed in #3). I have no Jira/Atlassian tool available in this session, so I could not pull SFCC-847's AC text from the source of record directly. What I can confirm from this repo: the PR's own story file (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:49-57`) independently paraphrases the same AC in the author's own words — "the 'Selected' variant renders the chosen value as a chip/tag replacing the options list... its placement inside the accordion body are open [pending sign-off]" — which matches the claim's quoted wording closely and is itself evidence the AC exists and reads that way. Given that corroboration plus the confirmed code behavior, the implementation is the inverse of what's described (chip-on-collapse vs. AC's chip-inside-expanded-replacing-list). What would fully settle it: the literal SFCC-847 AC text pulled from Jira.

**11. Accordion width vs. drawer-content, code side only — CONFIRMED (as scoped).**

| D | `{label, variant:'social', icon, role:'checkbox', ariaChecked:true}` | **ERROR** TS2353 "'role' does not exist in type 'ZimmSocialButtonProps'" |
| E | `{label, role:'tab'}` (invalid literal) | **ERROR** TS2322 |

| G | `{label, variant:'primary'}` | no error (valid) |

Modelled as a discriminated // — e.g. a filter chip. Without these a screen reader announces the control as a plain // Toggle semantics, for a button that represents a *selectable state* rather than an action`

Without these a screen reader announces the control as a plain button and never conveys whether it is currently applied. Modelled as a discriminated union so the role and its state cannot be supplied apart: a `role="checkbox"` with no `aria-checked` is a selectable control that never exposes what it is set to."), confirming this is a mechanical mangling (likely a Prettier collapse or bad merge), not intentional. content.text:
Correction first: **I was wrong to say I'd killed the social-icon finding.** I measured `/login`, which renders a different, older button. The changed code path only appears in the wishlist sign-in drawer, and I couldn't get that drawer to open on the preview. So that one is back to **unconfirmed either way** — three agents reached it independently from source (one read Chakra's icon defaults directly), and I have no browser evidence against it. It's excluded from everything below.

Now, the four decisions.

---

## Question 1 — the two big ones

**The filter-loss bug.** A shopper filters Dresses by Black. They open Filters, poke at Category, click Tops, think better of it, click Dresses again, hit Apply. Black is gone. They never touched Colour.

Why it happens: when you change category, the code throws away every filter you'd buffered, because changing category usually *should* reset them. But it only asks "is this different from what I last clicked?" — never "am I back where I started?" So clicking away and back reads as two real changes, and the second one leaves you with an empty basket of filters that then overwrites the live URL.

He already wrote the function that fixes this. It's called `resyncPendingRefine`, it's unit-tested, and it's pulled into the page — and then never called. Lint says so out loud.

**Why it matters more than it looks:** this is a wrong-results bug, not a cosmetic one. The shopper sees a product grid they didn't ask for and has no reason to distrust it.

**The store filter.** "Show me what's available at my boutique" used to sit on the PLP in both desktop and mobile. It's gone. Not descoped, not mentioned — the code that powers it is still sitting there, just with nothing rendering it. The feature still works in the header and on PDP, so it's now missing from the one page whose whole job is filtering.

The difference between these two: the first is clearly a bug. The second might be a deliberate call he made while ripping out the old sidebar and just didn't write down. That's why the options split them.

**My read:** block on the first, ask about the second.

---

## Question 2 — the drawer recipe

Someone else already fought this exact fight. Back on 12 September, on the Wishlist/Login work, the mobile drawer header was measured in a real browser, found to be 72px when Figma wanted 80px, changed to 80px, and signed off. Twenty-two lines of comment recorded who measured it, against which Figma node, which consumers it affected, and that it was approved.

This PR sets it back to 72px and deletes those twenty-two lines. Plus two more comment blocks of the same kind — about thirty lines of "here's why this number is this number" gone.

Three live things use that header on mobile: this new filter drawer, the Wishlist/Login drawer on real phones, and the country/language prompt. Two of those belong to other people's tickets. Nothing tests the value, so every gate stays green.

**Two separate problems, and they need separating:**
1. A number owned by another ticket changed without that ticket's owner in the room.
2. The evidence trail was erased, so the next person has nothing to push back with and this can ping-pong forever. Our own rules say don't delete comments unless you're deleting the code they describe — the constant stayed, only the value moved.

**The tension:** he may be right that 72px is correct now. SFCC-926 might genuinely have changed the spec. But that's a conversation with the Wishlist/Login owner, not a quiet edit inside a PLP PR.

**My read:** the third option. Show the evidence, cite the rule, ask him which way to resolve — because I don't actually know whether 80 or 72 is right, and neither does he without talking to that owner.

---

## Question 3 — the smaller ones

**Empty accordions.** Three filter sections open to nothing, on every product list page. I pulled the live API: Business Manager returns those three facets with zero values. So the missing data is SFCC-104's fault, and that ticket is Blocked — not his. But his code turns *every* facet the API returns into a section without checking it has anything in it. One line fixes it. Worth posting precisely *because* it's cheap and the framing is fair to him.

**No screen-reader announcements.** Press Apply, the whole grid changes, and a screen reader says nothing. Same for removing a chip or paging through them. The ticket has an explicit accessibility criterion covering this. Worth noting: the phrase "accessible filter announcements" comes from CodeRabbit's auto-summary, not from him — so this is a gap, not him claiming something he didn't do.

**Checkboxes vs radio buttons.** The criteria say Category should be radio buttons. He shipped checkboxes that behave like radios. Sighted users won't notice. A screen-reader user gets told these are independent tick-boxes, so nothing signals that picking one un-picks the last. He imported the radio components and never used them, so he started one way and switched. Worth asking which is right rather than telling him — partly because *he* raised a multi-select proposal on the ticket that nobody ever answered.

**Story exports and the scrambled comment.** Two story files are missing the export our own rules require. And the comment explaining his best idea in this PR — the toggle-semantics type — has its sentences concatenated in the wrong order and reads as nonsense. Both trivial, both a two-minute fix. The only question is whether you want the review to carry small stuff alongside the serious stuff.

---

## Question 4 — the things that aren't his fault

**Figma.** Kiera posted "Designs are done" with a link. That link opens a frame called "Footer SEO Expand." It is not the filter drawer. The only real spec I could find covers the collapsed desktop state and nothing else — no expanded facets, no Selected state, no mobile. He built most of this with no design to build against, and I reviewed most of it with no design to review against. That's worth fixing before the next person hits it.

**The ticket itself.** Jira automatically bounced SFCC-847 on 16 September for failing its Definition of Ready. The PR was opened about an hour later. The ticket is still "In Progress." And back on 9 September the reporter agreed to move several criteria off this story onto SFCC-108 — that never happened, so the description and the criteria now contradict each other about what this story even covers. A lot of the scope drift in this PR reads like a direct consequence.

**The stale rules file.** `overrideStyling.md` describes three button constants as living in the button recipe. They don't exist anywhere and haven't for a while. It's a Tier 1 doc that loads into every session, so it's quietly misinforming everyone, including me at the start of this review.

---

One thing worth weighing across all four: **this PR can't merge right now anyway** — develop has moved eight commits past it and it conflicts. Whatever we ask for, he has to rebase first, and the diff may shift.
